- When sentiment is consistently bullish (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for 1–3 day horizons.
- After sharp price spikes (≥5% from prior peak), model often overshoots; apply a 2–5% downward correction in next 3–5 days.
- If sentiment turns bearish (≤0.33) after a rally, model fails to adjust quickly; reduce forecast by 1–4% for 2–5 day horizons.
- When news volume drops to 0 for 2+ consecutive days, model overconfidently holds high forecasts; reduce by 2–5% for 3–7 day horizons.
- Model underestimates when sentiment is volatile (±0.33 change) and news volume is low; add 0.5–2% to forecast for 1–3 day horizons.
- For 30-day forecasts, model often misses mean reversion; if 18-day history shows strong trend, adjust forecast toward 10–15% of recent average, not extreme highs/lows.
- If sentiment change is negative and news volume is high, model tends to lag; add 0.5–2% to forecast for 1–3 day horizons to compensate for lag.
